minutes.headline: Water commissioners deferred a proposed Zone 2 bylaw change, discussed the Hickory Hills appeal, and weighed moving idle cash into higher-interest accounts.
minutes.summary: The commissioners reviewed a planning-board-sponsored Zone 2 bylaw rewrite based on DEP's model language and agreed to push it to the next meeting for more review, also wanting the Zone 2 map expansion pursued with it. They discussed a residents' appeal of the Conservation order for the Hickory Hills pilot study, the Mass Ave water main permitting difficulties, and a proposal to move idle bank funds into higher-yield accounts. Only the prior minutes were voted, plus adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was offered.

budget_items.topic: Mass Ave water main replacement cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Delays reportedly pushed the project cost far above the first proposal, and delays add cost that falls on ratepayers.

budget_items.topic: On-site engineer inspection for Mass Ave main
budget_items.what_was_said: DOT requires an on-site professional engineer, adding to cost via a new proposal.
Large balances earn nothing and wire fees are charged; Enterprise offered to waive fees and move two accounts to higher rates.
A small account receiving cell-lease income could be moved into a six-month FDIC-enhanced CD; the board favored about a million in CDs.
The district may look at a stipend for employees who opt out of its health insurance, modelled on a town trial.
Staff wants aging equipment replaced and a backhoe-vs-rubber-tired excavator cost comparison; a water main/equipment account exists.

decisions.decision: Zone 2 bylaw proposal pushed to the next meeting under old business for further review; copy of the old bylaw requested.
Board wants the Zone 2 map expansion for the well pushed alongside the bylaw change and asked staff to check that planning considered other Zone 2s.
Superintendent to contact DEP (water and conservation sides) and the Conservation chair regarding the Hickory Hills appeal.
110 Bird Street struck from the agenda; pilot study, water main and health insurance stay on old business.
Treasurer to talk to Rollstone about rates before closing or moving accounts; board favored shifting idle funds into higher-yield accounts.
Staff asked to make a list of equipment needed for replacement.

what_happened.line: The commissioners pushed a proposed Zone 2 bylaw rewrite to the next meeting for more review and asked for a copy of the old bylaw.
The board wants the Zone 2 map expansion for the well pursued alongside the bylaw change, and asked staff to check whether planning considered other Zone 2s.
The superintendent was asked to contact DEP and the Conservation chair about a residents' appeal of the order covering the Hickory Hills pilot study.
The board favored moving idle bank funds into higher-yield accounts; the treasurer will talk to Rollstone about rates before any account is closed or moved.
The only votes were approval of the prior minutes and adjournment; staff were asked to list equipment needing replacement.

why_it_matters: A Zone 2 bylaw sets what can be built over the land that recharges the town's well, so the wording and map the district backs affect land use near the water supply.
Delays on the Mass Ave water main and added inspection requirements add cost that, as discussed, falls on water ratepayers, and idle cash earning little is money the district could put to work.
watch_next: The Zone 2 bylaw returns under old business at the next water commissioners' meeting.
The treasurer's report back on Rollstone rates, and the staff list of equipment to replace.
